correctness.rationale: In arbitrary ambient dimensions the tangent correction lives in the two factor planes. Its exact two-by-two matrix [[cd,cb],[ad,0]] yields simple leading singular value and strict angle contractions. Boundary cases give either zero projection, one-step termination or two-step termination. In target bases, exact Gram offdiagonals are a*b^2*c^3 and a^2*b*d^3, yielding the cubic recurrences; the logarithmic linearization has eigenvalues three and minus one, so the matrix error has the precise base-three double-log rate. The 15,310 executed exact and floating-point assertions supplement but do not substitute the proof.

originality.rationale: Exact comparison shows that [1] establishes the SVD-retracted update and local quadratic random-sensing results, but not the identified full-observation all-start basin with a sharp cubic precision exponent. The population identity in [2, Lemma 5.3] uses orthographic rather than SVD retraction and does not imply this orbit. The survey [3] and RGD study [4] likewise do not imply it. Residual priority risk: an unindexed specialized deterministic SVD-retraction analysis could cover the calculation.
residual_risks: An unindexed population-dynamics proof for truncated-SVD rank-one Riemannian Gauss–Newton could imply this result.
The older general Gauss–Newton convergence article was available only at abstract-level in this comparison, and specialized appendices could contain stronger formulae.
The present result is a particular exact observation model, not a claim of novelty for all geometric Gauss–Newton methods.

value.rationale: A complete all-start basin and sharp cubic rate for the exact full-observation specialization of an emerging SVD-retracted low-rank Gauss–Newton method provide a natural deterministic control problem. They expose a single geometric degeneracy and isolate the rate-changing contribution of SVD retraction, a substantive distinction from the known orthographic population identity. They furnish a rigorous baseline for future perturbation and partial-observation analyses; no transfer to those settings is claimed.
